thesis_summary: Short Valero vs long equal-weight energy at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week ratio. 2026's record crack spreads are a war premium from the Strait of Hormuz blockade; both Washington and Tehran now publicly say a reopening deal is close (FT, Aug 4: blockade lifted + Iranian export curbs eased in exchange). VLO at 6.9x EV/EBITDA on peak war-driven earnings has the most to give back when cracks normalize.
thesis_detail: The numbers: VLO/RSPG ratio sits at 2.9004 vs a 52-week range of 1.799-2.984 and a median of 2.191 — the 93rd percentile. VLO is +55% over six months, +27% in three, massively outperforming every non-refiner in coverage. The driver is not structural: gas prices +98% YTD vs WTI +44% (Forbes, Jul 23) because the US naval blockade of Hormuz (reimposed July after the June ceasefire collapse) cut product supply while US refiners ran at up to 95% utilization (Reuters). That is peak-margin, peak-utilization, peak-multiple pricing. The catalyst is now dated: CNN (Aug 5) reports a Hormuz deal could land 'by Friday'; AP and WaPo confirm both sides say terms are close; the FT-reported framework (lift blockade, ease Iranian oil export restrictions for a reopening) is doubly bearish for the refiner complex — it restores crude supply AND collapses the product scarcity premium that is 100% of the 2026 refiner outperformance. Valuation check: VLO at 6.9x trailing EV/EBITDA and 10.8x forward PE on what are almost certainly cycle-peak earnings; MPC (7.6x, 88th pctile ratio, and already rolling over from 2.98 to 2.90 over the last 10 sessions) confirms the complex is stalling at the highs. Positioning: refiners are the crowded energy long of 2026. Even a partial Oman-brokered arrangement (CBS, Aug 6: 'close, but not full reopening') starts the margin normalization; post-Labor Day demand fade and September turnaround season add a seasonal tailwind to the short. Stop is a new 52-week ratio high — if the deal collapses a third time and cracks rip to new records, the thesis is wrong and we take the small loss.
variant_perception: Consensus is extrapolating record cracks (analyst price targets still chasing the stocks higher post-Q2 beats; MPC raised its buyback). The desk's variant view: the war premium embedded in product prices is a political decision away from evaporating, and both principals are now publicly negotiating the endgame. The market prices maybe 40% probability of a near-term deal; the FT-sourced framework and the 'by Friday' rhetoric from the US side put it higher, and the asymmetry at the 93rd percentile ratio is extreme — roughly 4% risk to a new high vs 15%+ to median reversion.
catalyst: Strait of Hormuz reopening deal (US-Iran/Oman track) — reported close as of Aug 4-5 with terms already leaked; secondary: weekly EIA product inventory builds as post-Labor Day gasoline demand fades and September refinery turnarounds begin.
catalyst_timeline: 1-4 weeks for the Hormuz headline; 2-6 weeks for crack normalization to show in estimates
key_risks: Hormuz deal collapses a third time (June ceasefire precedent; Iran denies direct US talks; Houthi tanker attack Aug 5) — cracks make new records and the ratio blows through the 2.984 high
Structural product tightness persists: pre-war Gulf Coast utilization was already 93-95% with elevated distillate margins (Dallas Fed), so cracks may normalize only partially, capping ratio downside
Gulf Coast hurricane season supply shock sends cracks higher regardless of geopolitics
VLO/MPC buyback programs ($4.4B MPC authorization) cushion the shorts on any dip
Crude-side view belongs to the Commodities seat: if a deal crashes WTI hard, the RSPG long leg absorbs E&P pain — pair is not fully insulated from the crude leg of the trade
